newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UBS still rates SBC as a "buy".
newsitem.headline: UBS still rates SBC as a "buy".

text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland UBS (UBS) said it still favours Swiss Bank Corp (SBC) as a "buy" in a model investment portfolio.

"In view of significant cost-cutting potential in the bank's Swiss business, a favourable medium-term profit outlook and the continued attractivness of its shares, SBC remains our favourite in the sector," UBS said in an analysis.
The analysis follows SBC's announcment of a major restructuring on Wednesday.
UBS said that measures announced by SBC on Wednesday had a medium-term cost-savings potential of around 400 million Swiss francs per annum.
The measures include, in the next three years, a reduction of 1,700 jobs, or 13 percent of SBC's domestic workforce, and closure of 80 retail branch banks out of an existing 325.
UBS said the restructuring of SBC's "less profitable" domestic business would allow it to achieve a sustained increase in earnings power.
UBS also said that a radical change in the way in which SBC will calculate its provisions will make risks in its credit business easier to assess.

SBC said Wednesday it will switch to a new loan-loss provisioning method in which it will take an initial recurring charge of about 600 million Swiss francs in its annual consolidated income statement.

The amount represents about 0.5 percent of the average loan volume. A one-time general loan-loss reserve will be charged to its 1996 consolidated income statement totaling 2.0 billion Swiss francs. The amount compared with what SBC said is an expected group net profit, after tax, of about 1.4 billion Swiss francs.
UBS analysts forecast an after-tax net of 1.370 billion francs for 1996, excluding extraordinary charges and excluding minority holdings, and a comparable net of 1.760 billion for 1997.
